names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 17 martie.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 17 Μαρτίου, «Άγιος Μαρίνος», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's second heading for the Julian 17 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Свети мученик Марин.“, with the rank words Свети мученик left off. The heading gives no epithet and no city, so the bare forename is what the source gives; no other folder in the corpus holds a Serbian Марин.

Read out of the name link behind days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 17 марта ст. ст., «Марин Кесарийский (Палестинский), мч.», with the rank word left off. The link gives the city and the province, which none of this folder's other three forms has; the day's own line gives the name alone, declined to «Марина».

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 17 марта ст. ст. — «Мч. Марина (260).»

attestations.note: The julian 17/3 is the same menologion day the other three calendars keep him on. The line closes with a year, 260, where the Ohrid Prologue gave only the third century; 260 falls inside that century, so the year is taken and the century stays in the note beside it. His life page lists a second day, «7 августа», which this calendar's 17 марта page does not repeat; it is recorded here and the folder does not render on it. The day page prints no hymn under his name.

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul zilei pentru 17 martie — «Sfântul Mucenic Marin»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 17ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιος Μαρίνος»

attestations.note: «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 17 Μαρτίου εκάστου έτους.» The page gives him no year, no country and no persecutor: «Ο Άγιος Μαρίνος έζησε στα χρόνια των διωγμών της Εκκλησίας» — he lived in the years of the persecutions of the Church. It prints a couplet over him and no hymn, so no dates object is written from this reading.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 30.03.2026 (17. март ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Марин.“

attestations.note: The day's second and last entry, on the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek already keep in this folder, and the only one of the three pages to say anything about him at all: he was a soldier, he not only refused to offer sacrifice to the idols but scattered the sacrifices others had offered and trampled them underfoot, and for that he was tortured and beheaded in the third century. The folder held no date of any kind and now holds that century for his death. `soldier` is added to `types` from the entry's own words „Био војник“, which is BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §5's mapping of Војник. A senator Asterius is named in the body — he was so moved by the courage Christ gives his followers that he carried the martyr's body away on his own back and buried it honourably, and the heathen killed him too as a Christian — and he takes no row and no folder: the heading names only Marinus, the corpus keeps no Asterius who was read as this senator, and a person the body names is recorded here rather than made a folder, as this wave has done since the bishop Peter of the Forty. The stored form is the bare forename, because Свети мученик is the rank and the heading gives nothing else. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

death.note: Two calendars, and the Russian one is the more exact without contradicting the other. The Ohrid Prologue for the Julian 17 March: „Због тога беше мучен и посечен, у III веку.“ days.pravoslavie.ru closes its line for 17 марта ст. ст. with «(260)», which falls inside that century, so the year is taken and the century is not contradicted. The Russian life page gives no year of its own.
